processing_time: Normally 15 calendar days after the application is lodged; can be extended to up to 45 days in individual cases. Apply at least 15 days and no earlier than 6 months before the trip.
validity: Up to 90 days in any 180-day period
notes: Common Schengen rules apply (France is a Schengen member). Apply online on the official France-Visas portal (france-visas.gouv.fr), then submit at the external visa centre it directs you to; a separate service charge is payable there. The visa centre provider and its service charge in India could not be confirmed from an official page during verification, so confirm both on France-Visas. Under the EU's April 2024 'cascade' rules for Indian nationals applying in India, someone who has obtained and lawfully used two Schengen visas in the previous three years can normally get a 2-year multiple-entry visa, normally followed by a 5-year one if the passport is valid long enough. Since 10 April 2026 the EU Entry/Exit System (EES) records non-EU short-stay travellers' entries and exits digitally (facial image; visa holders' fingerprints are already on file) instead of passport stamps.
documents: Passport valid for at least 3 months after the planned departure from the Schengen area
Completed visa application (via France-Visas)
Recent passport-sized photo
Travel medical insurance covering emergency medical care, hospitalisation and repatriation (minimum cover €30,000)
Proof of accommodation and travel itinerary
Proof of sufficient funds (e.g. bank statements)
Proof of employment / leave letter or other ties to India

processing_time: Normally 15 calendar days after the application is lodged; can be extended to up to 45 days in individual cases. Apply at least 15 days and no earlier than 6 months before the trip.
validity: Up to 90 days in any 180-day period
notes: The Schengen area has 29 countries: 25 EU member states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland (Bulgaria and Romania became full members on 1 January 2025). Apply at the consulate of the country where you will spend the longest time; if stays are equal, apply to the country you will enter first. Visa centres charge a separate service fee. Under the EU's April 2024 'cascade' rules for Indian nationals applying in India, someone who has obtained and lawfully used two Schengen visas in the previous three years can normally get a 2-year multiple-entry visa, normally followed by a 5-year one if the passport is valid long enough. Since 10 April 2026 the EU Entry/Exit System (EES) records non-EU short-stay travellers' entries and exits digitally instead of passport stamps.
documents: Passport valid for at least 3 months after the planned departure from the Schengen area
Completed visa application form
Recent passport-sized photo
Travel medical insurance covering emergency medical care, hospitalisation and repatriation (minimum cover €30,000)
Proof of accommodation and travel itinerary
Proof of sufficient funds (e.g. bank statements)

processing_time: Decisions on C visas are generally reached within 15 calendar days (Embassy of Italy, New Delhi); some cases take longer. Under EU rules this can be extended to up to 45 days.
validity: Up to 90 days in any 180-day period
notes: Italy is a Schengen member, so common Schengen rules apply. Applications are submitted through VFS Global (Italy's outsourcing agency) and decided by the Italian Embassy's visa section or the consulate covering your region. The Embassy collects the fee in INR at an exchange rate it adjusts periodically, and VFS Global charges a separate service charge; check the current INR amounts on the VFS Global Italy page. Fees are not refunded if the visa is refused. Indian nationals can benefit from the EU's 2024 'cascade' for multi-year multiple-entry visas after lawful use of previous Schengen visas.
documents: Passport valid for at least 3 months after the planned departure from the Schengen area
Completed Schengen visa application form
Recent passport-sized photo
Travel medical insurance covering emergency medical care, hospitalisation and repatriation (minimum cover €30,000)
Proof of accommodation and travel itinerary
Proof of sufficient funds (e.g. bank statements)

processing_time: Usually a decision within 3 weeks after the biometric appointment. You can apply up to 3 months before you travel; faster decision services may be available for an extra fee.
fee: £135 (up to 6 months). Long-term visitor visas: £506 (2 years), £903 (5 years), £1,128 (10 years)
validity: Up to 6 months per visit (long-term visas also allow up to 6 months per visit)
notes: The UK is not part of Schengen, so a separate visa is needed. Apply online on GOV.UK, then attend a visa application centre appointment to give biometrics.
documents: Passport valid for the whole of the stay
Online visa application
Evidence you can support yourself (and any dependants) during the trip, e.g. bank statements
Evidence you will leave the UK at the end of the visit, e.g. proof of employment / leave letter
Travel itinerary and accommodation details

visa_type: Tourist visa arranged before travel (most Indian passport holders); entry visa for Indian nationals holding certain residence permits
processing_time: No official processing time is published for tourist visas arranged through airlines, hotels or travel agents; it varies by channel.
fee: Pre-arranged tourist visa: varies by sponsoring channel (airline, hotel or travel agent). Entry visa for eligible residence-permit holders: AED 100 (14 days) or AED 250 (60 days)
validity: Depends on the tourist visa issued. Entry visa for eligible permit holders: 14 days (extendable once) or 60 days (single entry, not extendable)
notes: Indian ordinary passport holders are NOT visa-free for the UAE. Most need a tourist visa arranged before travel, through a UAE-based airline (e.g. Emirates, Etihad, flydubai), a licensed travel agent or hotel, or online via ICP / GDRFA Dubai. UAE embassies do not issue tourist visas. Exception (ICP, 25 June 2026): Indian nationals with a valid residence permit from the USA, an EU member state, the UK, Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand or Canada can get a 14-day entry visa (AED 100, extendable once) or a 60-day visa (AED 250, single entry, not extendable); the overstay fine is AED 50 per day. GDRFA's service page for this route requires the passport and the permit/green card to be valid for at least 6 months. Older official pages also listed a valid US visit visa as qualifying, but ICP's June 2026 announcement mentions only residence permits, so travellers relying on a US visit visa alone should confirm with ICP or their airline. A self-sponsored 5-year multiple-entry tourist visa (90 days per visit, extendable once by 90 days) is open to all nationalities. It requires a bank balance of USD 4,000 or equivalent over the last six months, UAE-valid health insurance and an onward or return ticket.
documents: Passport valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry
Recent photo (white background)
Return or onward ticket
Hotel booking or host details (as required by the sponsoring airline, hotel or agent)
For the residence-permit route: a valid residence permit / green card from one of the qualifying countries

processing_time: Interview appointment wait times vary by consulate and change often; check the State Department's official appointment wait-time tool. An optional expedited-appointment fee of $750 (from 1 July to 31 December 2026, selected posts only) can secure an interview within 10 business days.
validity: Visa validity and number of entries follow the State Department's reciprocity schedule for India; the length of each stay is decided by US border officers on entry
notes: Fill in the online DS-160, pay the fee and book an in-person interview. Since 1 October 2025 almost all applicants, including children under 14 and adults over 79, need an in-person interview; limited waivers exist for some renewals of full-validity B visas within 12 months of expiry. Book the interview at the US Embassy or Consulate in your country of residence or nationality. In India the fee is paid in rupees at the embassy's consular exchange rate (₹98 per US$1 from 25 May 2026). A $250 'visa integrity fee' became US law in July 2025, but its collection status could not be confirmed from an official page during verification, so check travel.state.gov before quoting a total.
documents: Valid passport
DS-160 confirmation page
Visa fee payment receipt / appointment confirmation
Recent photo meeting US visa photo requirements
Evidence of ties to India and of funds for the trip (e.g. employment, bank statements)

visa_type: Short-term stay visa for tourism (issued as a single-entry eVISA when applied through VFS Global in India)
processing_time: Minimum 5 working days from submission to the Embassy (VFS Global, Delhi). The Embassy says processing times can vary significantly and cannot be expedited. Applications are accepted from 3 months before travel.
fee: ₹500 visa fee for Indian nationals (single or multiple entry, from 1 July 2026), plus VFS service charge
validity: Single-entry eVISA for tourism; stays of up to 90 days (the Embassy decides the period granted)
notes: Since 1 April 2024 people residing in India can get Japan's eVISA (single-entry short-term tourist visa) by applying through VFS Global (Japan Visa Application Centre); no prior appointment needed. Only ordinary passport holders arriving by air (or by certain scheduled international ferries) are eligible. The eVISA 'Visa issuance notice' must be shown online at the airport; screenshots, PDFs and printouts are not accepted. The visa fee is charged only if the visa is issued, and VFS Global adds its own service charge (INR 800 per application on its Delhi page). Indian nationals may also be eligible for multiple-entry visas under Japan's relaxed rules for Indians. The Embassy's live site blocked automated access, so its fee and process details were read from a 1 September 2026 archived copy.
documents: Valid passport (ordinary)
Visa application form
Recent photo
Travel itinerary and proof of bookings
Proof of funds (e.g. bank statements)
Full checklist on the VFS Global Japan India page

visa_type: Visa exemption for tourism (up to 30 days)
fee: No visa fee under the visa exemption
validity: Up to 30 days per entry for tourism (for arrivals from 15 September 2026; it was 60 days before that)
notes: From 15 September 2026 Indian ordinary passport holders get a 30-day visa exemption for tourism under Thailand's revised scheme (Royal Gazette, 31 August 2026); the earlier 60-day exemption ended. Entries over land borders on this exemption are generally limited to two per calendar year. All foreign visitors must complete the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) online at tdac.immigration.go.th within 3 days before arrival; it is not a visa. For longer stays or other purposes, apply for a visa via Thailand's official e-Visa system (thaievisa.go.th). Immigration officers may ask for proof of onward travel or funds; those conditions were not confirmed from an official page during verification.
documents: Valid passport
Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) completed online within 3 days before arrival

visa_type: Visitor visa (subclass 600), Tourist stream (apply outside Australia)
processing_time: Varies; the Department of Home Affairs publishes a processing-time guide based on recently decided applications (a guide only, not specific to your application).
fee: AUD 250 per applicant (base application charge; concessions apply in limited circumstances)
validity: Stay of up to 12 months; the period granted is decided by the Department
notes: Apply online through ImmiAccount while outside Australia; you must also be outside Australia when the visa is decided. Each applicant, including each family member, pays separately, and there may be extra costs for health checks, police certificates and biometrics. You cannot extend this visa from inside Australia. You must have adequate arrangements for health insurance.
documents: Valid passport
Online application via ImmiAccount
Evidence of enough money for the stay (e.g. bank statements, pay slips, tax records)
Evidence of ties to India / intention to visit only
